title: Meet Agenticks, an AI quant-trading agent for research, backtesting, and automation WITHOUT needing to know code.
author: person-person12
selftext:
Today, [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/algoagent) lets a no-code trader **describe a strategy in plain English,** turn it into testable code, **backtest** it on historical data, inspect every trade, and either choose to make an indicator for TradingView, or automate it live to their broker. Nine months ago, that same product was **WealthLearn**, and Reddit was right to say it was too hard to understand.   
  
[The last time I posted here](https://www.reddit.com/r/ai_trading/s/EJxPLmqFI1), I explained **WealthLearn** by listing everything our team had built: **market research, backtesting, TradingView indicators, a stock screener, AI forecasts, broker connections, strategy automation, a market terminal, education, portfolio tools, and a separate futures application.** 

It was a long list because we had spent roughly **nine months** building a lot of real capability, but the list was also the problem.

The post went viral, and people had fair questions about the **backtest engine, the role of AI, overfitting, broker execution, pricing, data quality,** and whether this was just another model wrapped in a nice interface. I answered most of those questions from inside the architecture because our team knew how everything connected, but what we had not accepted yet was that a new user could not see that connection.

To them, **WealthLearn** looked like a stock screener, a portfolio builder, a market terminal, several AI products, a TradingView tool, a learning platform, and an automation system that happened to share one login.

Every part had a reason to exist, but the product did not have a clear answer to a much simpler question:

>

That was the **useful criticism.**

# -----------

# Why we rebuilt it

We went back through the **Reddit feedback**, spoke directly with users, and had the product experience audited. The same problem kept appearing: people did not need us to prove that we could build another tool, they needed the tools we had already built to feel like **one understandable product.**

So we rebuilt it around **one clear process**, and **WealthLearn became Agenticks.**

The name is simply **agents plus market ticks, stock tickers, and analytics.**, but more importantly, it now fits what the product has become.

The platform is organized around **four steps:**

1. **Research the idea.**
2. **Build the rules.**
3. **Validate the evidence.**
4. **Automate the strategy.**

# -----------

# What this looks like in practice

Imagine I trade an **opening-range breakout on QQQ** and want to know whether the rules I use have actually performed well historically.

In the old WealthLearn, I would have needed to know **which product to open, which page contained the relevant data, whether I was creating a study or a strategy, and where the result was supposed to go afterward.**

In **Agenticks**, I can ask:

>

That begins as a normal request written in **plain English.** Agenticks turns those words into **code**, checks that the rules are complete, runs the strategy using **historical market data**, and returns the evidence.

The result is not limited to a **win rate** and a large percentage at the top of the screen. It can include **every trade, drawdowns, return distribution, outliers, market regimes, parameter sensitivity, trading costs, Monte Carlo analysis,** and the exact rules responsible for the result.

If the evidence looks worth continuing, I can say:

>

That strategy can then move into **monitoring, paper testing, TradingView, alerts, or broker automation** including majors supported connections like WealthSimple, without having to be rebuilt in another product.

That is the main difference. The work now moves from **an idea, to code, to evidence, to a usable strategy** inside the same product.

# -----------

# What the AI actually does

There was a recurring mix-up in the last thread that I want to explain more clearly.

The AI is not sitting inside the backtest **predicting the next candle, inventing the return, or rewriting history after seeing the result.** At its simplest, the agent turns **words into code.**

You describe the strategy or research question, and it translates that request into the **rules and code required to test it.**

Coding agents can already build custom software from a description, but **statistical research and backtesting** cannot be treated like a completely open-ended coding project. A backtest has to ingest **market data correctly**, process that data in the correct order, avoid using future information, understand when enough historical data exists to calculate an indicator, and apply **entries, exits, stops, targets, sizing, sessions, trading costs, and position limits** consistently.

Every action also needs to be logged so the user can see exactly where the result came from.

That is why **Agenticks** does not give a model an empty coding window and hope the output works. Our internal tools provide the **market data, the required strategy and research formats, the testing tools, and the rules the agent has to follow while building.**

The code is checked before it runs, the platform controls what information is available during each point in the test, and the outputs are recorded in a format the rest of the product can inspect and use. If the work does not meet the required structure, it is rejected rather than producing a result that only looks convincing.

**We are not using AI to decide what the result should be.** We are using AI to turn an idea into code that a real testing system can run.

The same strategy version can then be used for **historical testing, monitoring, and supported live execution**, rather than having one piece of code for the backtest and something completely different running later. Any meaningful change creates a new version that has to be reviewed again.

Nobody should trust a strategy simply because **AI wrote it.** The value is that a trader can describe an idea, see the rules it becomes, test it properly, and understand the result without first having to learn how to program the entire thing themselves.

# -----------

# What is inside Agenticks now

The **Agent** is the main workspace. It can research markets, construct strategies, run historical studies, compare variations, retrieve saved work, read supported account context, and manage the movement from an idea into a tested or automated system.

# ------

# What the AI does

* **Research an idea** \- measures how a setup actually behaved on real market data.
* **Read the markets** \- live movers, sectors, news, GEX, and earnings.
* **Build a strategy** \- turns plain English into exact entry, exit, sizing, and risk rules.
* **Backtest it** \- full trade list, drawdowns, regimes, sensitivity, and costs, not just a win rate.
* **Stress-test risk** \- Monte Carlo and prop-firm pass odds on the actual trades.
* **Make a TradingView indicator** \- clean Pine Script v6 from a description.
* **Grade a stock or portfolio** \- outlook, volatility, drawdown, diversification, and overlap.
* **Read your accounts** \- read-only balances, holdings, and positions through connected brokers.
* **Automate a strategy** \- takes a tested strategy live on your broker, inside limits you set.
* **Place an order** \- prepared for your broker, you confirm before anything sends.

# ------

# Every other major platform feature

**The Agent** is the main workspace, where you describe an idea in plain English and it researches the market, writes the strategy rules, runs the backtest, and moves it toward monitoring or broker automation.

**AI Insights** gives daily, weekly, and monthly pre-market stock forecasts that call each name bullish or bearish, with previous outcomes tracked publicly.

**Research** covers stock and ETF screening, side-by-side comparisons, earnings, filings, news, sectors, and broader market context.

**Indicators** is a library of TradingView Pine Script v6 tools for volume profile, order flow, and level context.

**Terminal** is a live market terminal covering gamma exposure and dealer positioning, an order-flow stream, charting, news catalysts, nu performance, and market movers.

**Monitor** is a live view of your running algos, deployments, open positions, and P/L.

**Learn** covers backtesting, risk, market mechanics, and how to read the code the platform generates.

**Affiliates** is the referral program for earning on the people you bring to the platform.

This is still a lot of capability, but the difference is that users no longer have to understand our internal product map before they can use it.

# -----------

# What became easier

The biggest improvement is not the **name** or the **redesigned interface.** It is that the product now matches the way a trader actually thinks.

Most people do not begin by thinking about **strategy objects, data pipelines, or execution systems.** They begin with questions such as:

* **Does this pattern actually happen?**
* **What changes if I use 20 days instead of 50?**
* **Can you turn the way I trade into exact rules?**
* **Why did this strategy fall apart in 2022?**
* **Is the entire result dependent on three outlier trades?**
* **Can I get this into TradingView?**
* **Can this run automatically with the limits I choose?**

Those questions are now the interface.

A newer trader can understand what is happening without being buried in infrastructure, while a technical user can still inspect the **data source, parameters, strategy code, trade list, version history, risk controls, and assumptions.**

**Simpler does not have to mean less serious.**

# -----------

# Why we made the change

Our original goal was to make **advanced market research, testing, and systematic trading** more accessible to self-directed traders. Over time, that goal became overshadowed by how much infrastructure we were trying to provide.

Our team kept adding more capability, but the product became harder to operate and harder to explain. That tradeoff was not worth it.

Retail trading became easy to access long before **disciplined, systematic trading** became easy to understand. Someone can open a brokerage account and place an order in minutes, but that does not mean they can test an observation, define an invalidation, identify dependence on outliers, simulate risk, or turn a repeatable method into exact rules without learning multiple products and a programming language.

The person we are building for is not necessarily a **hedge-fund quant.** It is the self-directed trader or investor who has an observation, a method, or an idea and wants a serious way to ask:

>

That is what **Agenticks** is now.

# -----------

# The criticism was useful

The criticism on the last post helped our team get here, including some comments I did not enjoy reading at the time. Even where I disagreed with certain technical assumptions, the larger criticism was correct: we had built something capable, but we had not made that capability easy to understand.

I would genuinely like the **hard questions** again, especially from people who build backtest engines, trade systematic strategies, work with broker APIs, or have strong opinions about where an AI agent should stop and the testing system should begin.

>

**Disclaimer:** Agenticks provides self-directed research, strategy construction, testing, and software automation tools. Historical and simulated results do not predict future performance.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body:
**Good questions.**

**How the backtest works:**   
  
1) You work with the AI to research an idea first, it can spin up custom Python tests to check whether the edge is actually there before you commit to it (or if you already have a strategy in mind you can skip straight to defining your rules ***eg. entries, exits, filters, risk)***.   
  
2) Either way, once the rules are set the engine steps through historical bars one at a time and only acts on data that existed at that bar (so theres no lookahead).  
  
3) Each signal gets simulated as a real fill, then it tallies the results into expectancy, win rate, average R, max drawdown, and profit factor.   
  
4) On top of that it runs Monte Carlo (reshuffles the trade sequence to show the range of outcomes, not just the lucky path) and walk-forward (tests on data the strategy was never tuned on) so you can tell a real edge from a curve fit.

Data wise it's **10+ years across 10,000+ tickers (ingested for free via Alpaca API),** equities and ETFs, down to intraday. That's exactly why we don't touch yfinance as its intraday history caps out fast.

***On signup, we have heard a few issues which has since been fixed and have had signups coming in all morning. Give it another try and let me know if it still acts up.***

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body:
**We don't use Yahoo**, yfinance doesn't even offer intraday data beyond 90 days (max).  

We offer 10+ years and 10000+ tickers for just backtesting **along with...**

* **A deterministic Pine Script v6 compiler + fixer.** Multi-pass validator that generates and self-corrects TradingView scripts to compile clean every time (version gating, function-vs-variable rules, security-call args, balanced-paren checks). That's a real language toolchain, not an API wrapper.
* **A Python backtest engine that runs in isolated sandboxes.** Monte Carlo, walk-forward, expectancy/drawdown/SQN, plus a fidelity harness that proves the engine reproduces the same fills bar-for-bar (not "graph the price")
* **Columnar bar transport to fit huge datasets through execution limits.** Multi-symbol studies were blowing past the sandbox input cap, so bars move as columnar arrays (times + per-symbol OHLCV) and get rebuilt runtime-side. Thats legimate systems engineering 
* **Shared scheduled ingestion, not per-user API calls.** Cron jobs and shared cache tables feed the whole app so we're not hammering a provider per request. Bars live in chunked object storage and arent just dumped in Postgres.
* **Signed multi-broker live execution with fill reconciliation.** Real order routing across brokers with request signing and a reconciler that confirms fills. This is the part nobody vibecodes, because getting it wrong costs real money.
* **An agent that writes, runs, and backtests strategies in-chat** against your own broker's bars, with credit metering and tool orchestration behind it.

Not to mention our team of contract devs who I must give credit to for a ton of our progress.  But sure, we'll call it "vibe coded" lol
